newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bulls take breather then keep on running.
newsitem.headline: German bulls take breather then keep on running.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip IBIS DAX index put a brief round of profit-taking behind it on Friday and headed into the weekend back in bullish mood after higher than expected U.S. jobless data gave the stock market a lift.
The IBIS DAX-30 index penetrated the 3,400-point level after yo-yoing on the back of the U.S. data and ended the day at 3,419.51 points, up 0.68 percent or 22.96 points.
This was not far off a record of 3,441.51 points.
Earlier the DAX index, which tracks bourse trade in 30 German blue-chips, finished down 1.21 percent at 3,376.20 points.

"This is an entertaining market at the moment if you're on the right side of it, but at the same time it's difficult to trade on it. We took profit yesterday and this morning and then off we went again this afternoon, heading up," a trader said.
"I think we will keep tracking upwards next week. The demand for German stocks is very high at the moment and sentiment is generally positive," the trader said.

German shares traded lower during the morning, but following the publication of higher-than-expected February U.S. non-farm payroll figures, the market yo-yoed, falling 0.4 percent then rising to back above the key 3,400-point level.

"The reaction to the U.S. data just showed how this market wants to go up, and this kind of yo-yoing is becoming standard in this market. Stocks are moving a few percent every day it seems, and the market is getting used to that," a trader said.
The dollar traded very close to the 1.72-marks level which gave exporters a boost, chemical stocks in particular.
Hoechst AG ended up 32 pfennigs at 78.31 marks, BASF AG ended up 11 pfennigs at 64.41 marks while Bayer AG closed the day up 1.93 marks at 74.95 marks.
Shares in engineering group Deutz AG ended up 27.51 percent at 10.80, off earlier highs.

The strong advance came after the Platow Brief newsletter reported that Deutz, formerly Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG and rescued in a one-billion mark bail-out last year, would forecast a profit at its annual results conference of May 15.

Preference shares in medical products group Fresenius AG closed up 14 marks at 387 marks. Earlier the share fell over 2.5 percent after the group denied media reports that it planned to issue bonus shares.
Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank were also among the heaviest traded stocks. Deutsche ended up 46 pfennigs at 92.29 marks, while Commerzbank closed up 30 pfennigs at 44.50 marks.
